text: After the service, the people hurried out of the meeting house, some gathering in little circles to whisper and others walking home alone, wrapped in silent thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Squire Saunders, doubtless by an accidental lapse of memory, neglected to invite Mister Hooper to his table, where the good minister had blessed the food almost every Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> How strange, said the doctors wife, that a simple black veil, such as any woman might wear on her bonnet, should become so terrible on Mister Hoopers face. <break time="0.8s" /> That afternoon Mister Hooper attended the funeral of a young lady, and as he bent over the coffin, his veil hung straight down from his forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> Had her eyelids not been closed forever, the dead maiden might have seen his face, and he hastily caught back the veil as if fearing her glance. <break time="0.8s" /> A superstitious old woman, the only witness of this wonder, declared that at the instant when the ministers features were disclosed, the corpse had slightly shuddered. <break time="0.8s" /> That night, at the wedding of the handsomest couple in Milford, his veil cast such a gloom over the party that the joyful evening seemed like a funeral. <break time="0.8s" /> When he raised a glass of wine and caught sight of his own figure in the mirror, he shuddered, spilled the wine, and rushed out into the darkness.
